text: {"headline":"Provider 1000000027 bills 99215 well above risk-adjusted expectation at every complexity tier, including many low-complexity visits, but the few charts returned support the billed levels, so documentation is too thin to settle the question.","leaning":"inconclusive","interpretation":"The claims pattern leans toward concern. The 99215 share runs roughly three to four times the all-provider rate in every condition-count tier, not just among sicker patients. About a third of 99215s fall on patients with zero or one chronic condition, and the sampled low-complexity examples are mostly routine presentations: back pain (C0015212, C0015252), upper respiratory infection (C0015159, C0015888) and abdominal pain (C0015082, C0015427). The records review points the other way: none of the documented claims, including the five 99215s, were documented below the billed level (e.g., C0015130 and C0015743 are documented high MDM). However, five documented 99215s out of 167 billed is far too few to judge support, and most of the supported examples record no visit time. Only 2 of the 21 notes claiming moderate-or-higher data review lacked a lab or test line on the claim, so there is little sign of cloned or inflated notes in this small sample. A reviewer should first request charts specifically for the low-complexity 99215 claims listed in the packet. The aim is to see whether the documented MDM on simple acute complaints genuinely reaches high complexity or reads as templated."}
